title: Marked Section A practice and question-level analysis
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 58 (Marked Section A practice and question-level analysis (portal))
intro: Lesson 58: Section A review: targets and a wider reading plan. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

model.title: Journal entry on a travel article

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: 'A Night on the Ferry' (newspaper, 2026). Summary: a writer crosses at night and finds strangers sharing food. Quotation: 'the deck became a kitchen'; 'kitchen' suggests warmth and family. Attitude: grateful, surprised.

keywords.def: reading beyond set texts to build range
writing about real people, places and events
the main points in a few words
a record of what you read and think

questions.q: From your analysis, write your strongest and weakest Section A question

questions.a: For example: 'Explain the effect of every quotation.' 'End Q7 with a judgement.'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, build your own four-week wider reading plan and write one journal entry on an article from the reading list
questions.a: A plan matched to targets and a complete 60-word entry.

questions.q: Extend: add a speech from the list and note its audience and purpose
Stretch: choose two texts on one topic and plan a Q7 comparison
Which reading habit builds Section A skill most?
options: read, then write a short response on methods and attitude
only read fiction you already know
questions.a: A) read, then write a short response on methods and attitude. Active reading with a short written response practises the exam skills.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: what will you read this summer?
questions.a: A named text type with a reason.
